intro.h2: A Cary company that remodels bathrooms and nothing else
paragraphs: The Bath Remodeling Center, known for years as Portofino Tile, focuses on bathroom remodeling in Cary, NC and across the Triangle. That focus shows in the numbers: more than 2,000 bathroom remodels, over $15 million in completed projects and more than 25 years in the trade.

You work with an interior designer and licensed general contractor from the first measurement, and the company's own full-time employees handle every installation. The showroom on Ward Street in downtown Cary lets you compare tile, quartz and granite tops, vanities, shower glass and heated floors side by side before anything is ordered, with a designer beside you to explain how each choice performs.

services.h2: Bathroom remodeling in Cary, NC, from primary suites to hall baths

items.name: Primary and Master Bathrooms
items.blurb: Full primary bath remodels that start with layout: room at the vanity, how the shower opens, where towels go and whether the tub still earns its space. Master bath remodels are the most common topic in the firm's Google reviews, with 20 reviews tagged for it.

image.alt: Primary bathroom remodel in the Triangle with navy double vanities, built-in makeup desk, brass sconces and gray marble-look floor tile

items.name: Walk-in Showers and Tile
items.blurb: Custom showers with frameless glass, niches, benches and porcelain, glass or stone tile. Plenty of Triangle owners now trade a bulky soaking tub for a roomier shower that is simpler to clean and safer to step into. Glass enclosures are measured after tile and installed about three weeks later.

image.alt: Frameless glass walk-in shower with marble-look tile and bench beside a wood double vanity with arabesque tile wall and black fixtures

items.name: Tubs and Soaking Baths
items.blurb: Freestanding soakers, built-in tubs, jetted tubs and clawfoot styles, planned together with the shower so the room still works. If the household no longer needs a tub, the team talks through a conversion and what the existing plumbing connections allow.

image.alt: Freestanding white soaking tub next to a frameless glass shower with marble-look walls and plantation shutters in a remodeled bathroom

items.name: Vanities, Storage and Finishes
items.blurb: Custom-built vanities with drawers sized for daily items, quartz or granite tops, faucets, mirrors and medicine cabinets chosen together. A double vanity is planned to leave real counter space, not just a second sink. Heated floors can be added during design.

image.alt: Wood bathroom vanity with white top, backlit mirror, black towel warmer and frameless shower in a remodeled Triangle bathroom

why_choose_us.h2: Reasons Triangle homeowners book a showroom visit

items.title: Employees install your bath
items.text: Installations are done by the company's own full-time employees, not day-labor crews. Google reviewers call the craftsmen courteous and highly skilled and note the punctual crew and dust removal.

items.title: See it drawn before it is built
items.text: Nicole's CAD design process shows the finished room before work starts. You get clear written drawings and a written contract, so scope and selections are settled up front.

items.title: Free first steps
items.text: The first in-home visit, the first showroom appointment and a remodeling estimate are all free. The site notes that more extensive design consultations beyond those steps may carry a fee.

items.title: Voted best by neighbors
items.text: Local voters gave the firm Maggy Awards in 2025 and 2026 and Raleigh's Best 2025 honors from The News and Observer, including Gold for Kitchen and Bath Remodeler.

about.text: Nicole Fella studied interior design at the Fashion Institute of Technology in New York, then became a NASCLA licensed general contractor so she could manage the build as well as the look. She spent 11 years helping grow the company before taking over as owner of The Bath Remodeling Center, LLC, formerly Portofino Tile. Today the business identifies as women-owned and runs from a 5,000 square foot design center in downtown Cary. Clients name Nicole in their reviews, and some mention Bob from the team as well.

process.h2: How your bathroom remodel runs, step by step

steps.title: In-home measurements
steps.text: A free visit to measure the room, photograph what is there and hear what you want to keep or change.

steps.title: Showroom design session
steps.text: Plan the layout and pick tile, tops, cabinets and fixtures at the Ward Street showroom with your designer.

steps.title: Review the plans
steps.text: Go over the drawings, selections and estimate, including what is included and how changes would be handled.

steps.title: Written contract and drawings
steps.text: Sign a clear written contract with final drawings so you know the scope and schedule before demolition starts.

steps.title: Installation by employees
steps.text: Full-time installers complete most baths in 12 to 14 business days including inspections; frameless glass follows about three weeks later.

service_area.h2: Bathroom remodels across Wake, Durham and Orange counties
service_area.text: The showroom sits in downtown Cary, and most projects are in Cary, Apex and Raleigh. The team also travels to Holly Springs, Wake Forest, Rolesville, Clayton and Zebulon, and west to Durham, Chapel Hill, Carrboro and Hillsborough. Weekend and evening showroom visits are available by appointment. If your town is not listed, share your street address and the office will tell you if the crew can get there.

faq.h2: Bathroom remodeling questions we hear in Cary

items.q: How many days will we be without the bathroom?
items.a: The process page lists 12 to 14 business days for installation, including all inspections. Frameless shower glass is custom cut after tile is set and goes in about three weeks later. Your exact schedule depends on scope and product availability, and it is confirmed in writing before work begins.

items.q: What does the first visit cost me?
items.a: Nothing. The first in-home visit, the first showroom appointment and a complimentary remodeling estimate are all free. If you need more extensive design consultations beyond those steps, the site says a consultation fee may apply, so ask about it at your first meeting.

items.q: What affects the cost of a bathroom remodel?
items.a: Room size is only one factor. Moving the layout, the amount of plumbing and electrical work, cabinetry, tile and fixture choices all change the estimate. The team suggests listing your must-have changes first, then comparing alternatives together before you approve the scope.

items.q: Can you design a bathroom for aging in place?
items.a: Yes. Options include low-threshold or walk-in showers in place of a tub, room for a shower chair, a handheld showerhead and grab bars that match the other fixtures. Raise access needs early so entry design, clearances and fixture placement are part of the plan, not an add-on.

items.q: What should I bring to the showroom?
items.a: Bring photos of your current bathroom, rough room measurements if you have them, a list of priorities and pictures of styles you like. Mention whether easy access, storage, cleaning or keeping a bathtub matters most. Those details let the designer make the visit about your house.
